entities.summary: Janus Lascaris, also known as John Rhyndacenus, was a prominent Greek scholar in the Renaissance, whose scholarly contributions spanned the fields of Classics, Philosophy, and Linguistics. Born in Constantinople (modern-day Istanbul, Turkey) around 1460, Lascaris was a key figure in the revival of classical learning in Europe during the 16th century. His most notable achievement was the editing and translation of the Greek lexicon of Liddell-Scott-Jones, which became a foundational text for the study of Classics. Lascaris' work also had a significant impact on the development of modern linguistics, particularly in the field of philology. He was a member of the influential circle of scholars known as the 'Muses' in Constantinople, which brought together some of the most prominent minds of the time. Lascaris' legacy can be seen in the many scholars who built upon his work, including the renowned classical scholar and historian, Johann Ludwig Bachmann. As a scholar who was deeply rooted in the intellectual traditions of his time, Lascaris played a vital role in shaping the course of Western intellectual history.
